sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small species, very similar to and concolorous with M. boreus, from which it differs in the smaller head, compound eyes, ocelli and pronotum, the sparser head hairs, the shorter and more numerous hairs of the pronotum and abdomen, and the less distinctly narrowed sides of the pronotum. Posterior margin of the mesonotum broad, moderately deeply and widely notched; metanotum narrower and more sharply notched. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 7.50—7.75; body length without wings 4.25—4.75; head length (to apex of labrum) 0.97—0.99; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.57; head width 0.79—0.82; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.20—0.23; ocellus length 0.09; pronotum length 0.36—0.40; pronotum width 0.62—0.69; forewing length 5.70; forewing width 1.50.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Very small, mandibles very long and slender. Head (Fig. 334) and labrum orange reddish brown, mandibles uniformly reddish brown, antennae yellow ochraceous. Labrum long, widest at the base, rather sharply conical. Mandibles about as long as the head capsule, hardly widening at the base, extending almost straight to near the apex. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 2 about half as long as segment 1; segment 3 shortest. Measurements (mm): body length 5.00; head length with mandibles 2.40—2.62; head length (to clypeal suture) 1.41; head width 0.78; pronotum length 0.29; pronotum width 0.58.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original combination is Miorocerotermes leai Hill, 1927 (the OCR mostly reads leal). Measurements in mm. Distribution: Ooldea, South Australia (type locality). The original records that the species is known only from the type series; the Victorian and New South Wales series referred to this species in 1927 have been transferred to M. cavus. Type specimens: soldier holotype, alate and worker morphotypes in the South Australian Museum.
